core.title: Media details screen, resume playback and watchlist
covers: details screen with Play as default focus
core.guidance: Details: the primary action is Play (or Resume with the remaining time and a Start over alternative) and it takes default focus; metadata is a short scannable block (duration, year, rating, badges as text not colour), synopsis ≤3 lines with an expander, episodes as a rail or list with progress bars and the next unwatched episode preselected; secondary actions (watchlist, trailer, more like this) sit after Play in one row. Resume: a continue-watching row shows progress on each card, resumes at the saved position, and removes finished items; entering a title from the row returns focus to that card. Watchlist: one toggle with a clear on/off state and text label, works from cards and details, and is reflected immediately in the watchlist row. Everything is reachable with D-pad UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT and BACK returns to the row that launched the details.
core.use_when: Title/episode details, continue-watching rows, watchlist actions in a streaming or catch-up app.
core.avoid_when: Live-only channels without on-demand content (use the guide and player rules).

implementation.swiftui: tvOS: .prefersDefaultFocus on Play inside a focusScope; NavigationStack path keeps the row/card identity for restoration.

core.title: Horizontal rails (rows of content)
core.guidance: Each rail has a visible title, focused item scrolls to a fixed pivot (about 20–30% from the left) rather than centring, rails remember their last focused index when returning, row heights are consistent within a rail, and off-screen items are partially visible to signal continuation. Lazy-load rails and images; never render every rail on first paint. Keep the safe margin (~5% / 48 dp horizontal, 27 dp vertical at 960×540 dp).
core.use_when: TV browsing of categorised content: vertical axis moves between categories, horizontal axis moves within a category. The default TV home structure.
core.avoid_when: Fewer than ~8 items total (use a grid or list), or content that must be compared side by side.

implementation.swiftui: tvOS: ScrollView(.horizontal) with LazyHStack and .focusSection(); use .scrollTargetLayout for pivot behaviour.

guardrails.title: Every interactive colour has hover/pressed/focus/disabled/selected
covers: selected state visible and distinct from focus and hover
guardrails.guidance: Define state tokens per role (action.primary-hover/-pressed, bg.selected, text.disabled), keep label contrast on every state, make disabled visibly weaker but readable (≥3:1 recommended even though exempt), selected ≠ focused ≠ hovered. Dark theme redefines all of them.
guardrails.use_when: Buttons, links, list rows, tabs, chips, inputs, cards that are tappable, focus on TV.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never leave a state to the framework default on one platform and custom on another.
guardrails.selected_for: required coverage: visible focus, selected state visible and distinct from focus and hover

guardrails.title: TV: 10-foot typography
guardrails.guidance: Body ≥24 sp (Android) / ≥29 pt (tvOS) at 1080p design scale, captions ≥20 sp, titles 32–48, display 57–72; sans with large x-height and open counters; short strings (titles ≤2 lines, synopsis ≤3 lines with expansion); avoid thin weights (<400) and light text on busy imagery; line height ≥1.3.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never scale a desktop type ramp up by a factor; rebuild the scale for distance and for reduced text volume.
guardrails.selected_for: required coverage: accessibility, 10-foot typography, readable at distance

guardrails.title: TV: vertical = sections, horizontal = items
guardrails.guidance: Every focusable element must be reachable with straight UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT presses; no diagonal reasoning, no hidden hops. Search and settings live at a predictable edge. Grids: LEFT at the first column may enter side navigation, RIGHT at the last column stays. Forms: one field per row, DOWN advances.
guardrails.use_when: Any TV layout: rails, grids, menus, settings, forms.
guardrails.avoid_when: Avoid nested horizontal groups inside horizontal groups; avoid controls placed where no straight DPAD path reaches them.

guardrails.title: TV: overscan-safe margins
guardrails.guidance: Keep interactive and text content ≥5% from edges: at the 960×540 dp design frame that is 48 dp horizontal and 27 dp vertical (Android guidance: up to 58/28 dp for maximum safety; tvOS: 60 pt sides, 60 pt top/bottom on the 1920×1080 frame). Let rails scroll under the margin so partial cards hint at more content.
guardrails.use_when: All persistent UI (nav, titles, buttons, subtitles); backgrounds and artwork may bleed.
guardrails.avoid_when: Do not inset full-bleed imagery; do not rely on the panel reporting overscan.

guardrails.title: Virtualise long lists and tables
guardrails.guidance: Windowed rendering with stable row heights or measured heights, keyboard focus preserved when rows unmount (roving focus by key), aria-rowcount/aria-setsize so assistive tech knows the real size, scroll restoration on back navigation. Native: LazyColumn/List/FlatList/VirtualizingStackPanel already virtualise; keep keys stable.
guardrails.use_when: Lists/tables beyond a few hundred rows, grids of images, infinite feeds, EPGs.
guardrails.avoid_when: Small lists (<100) where virtualisation adds focus and find-in-page problems.
